_fixtureNote: CONSTRUCTED 2026-10-23. Venue x distance barrier priors as a 'preferredBand' and 'effectStrength' (0 = ignore, 1 = strong). Mostly qualitative evidence (low confidence); hard numbers noted where they exist. Learn real effects from the results store (>=300 races per venue) before trusting these over the generic prior.

1000-1200 (straight).note: No turns; sources conflict (wide = better ground vs inside bias on some days, e.g. 2026 Newmarket); lack of early tempo often favours on-pace runners. Use day-pattern lane bias.

1400-1600.note: Midfield draws 'most ideal'; penalise >=12 and 1-2 in big fields

2400-3200.note: Melbourne Cup 1958-2024: barrier 11 most wins (7); original-draw wins 1-8: 21, 9-16: 27, 17-24: 19

1000-1200.note: ~650m straight running before the home turn; inside advantage described as minimal (one guide disagrees)

1400-1600.note: Short run to first turn; barrier called 'the critical statistic' for the Caulfield Guineas

2400.note: Caulfield Cup since 1922: best barriers 8 wins each; barrier 1 one win (1941)

1000-1400.note: No statistics found; inside dominant when rail true, wide after rail moves / heavy

1600.note: Epsom: winner from double-digit gate in 12 of past 19; Doncaster: 12 of past 20 winners from barrier 10+

1800-2400.note: Long uphill straight rewards backmarkers; wide draws often not a hindrance

1000-1200.note: ~300m to first turn then ~200m before final bend; inside strongly favoured

1500-1600.note: Less influential than 1200m; an old newspaper claimed most mile winners came from near the outside

2040.note: Short run to first turn (Cox Plate trip)
